newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen firmer, led by retail buyers.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen firmer, led by retail buyers.

text.p: Sentiment for Singapore shares was seen firmer on Monday with dealers expecting retail buyers to remain active in the market.
"We've seen mainly retail interest recently and I think that will continue," one dealer at a local institution said.
"New listings are where the activity is," he added.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index closed up 6.83 points on Friday at 2,066.21.
Dealers said they were awaiting a statement from main board listed Osprey Maritime, the shipping firm at the centre of market rumours that it plans an acquisition in London.
Osprey issued a statement on Sunday which said talks "exploring the possibility of closer co-operation" with Gotaas-Larsen Ltd were in progress.
Osprey said it was requesting a suspension of trading in its shares from Monday morning.
